items.stem: A model has 92% overall accuracy but 70% recall for one subgroup. What does this show?

options.text: Aggregate accuracy can mask serious subgroup harm
options.rationale: Correct: disaggregated evaluation reveals hidden disparities.

options.text: The model is fair because overall accuracy is high
options.rationale: High aggregate accuracy does not imply subgroup fairness.

options.text: The dataset must be too small
options.rationale: Size is not what this result indicates.

items.explanation: Correct: disaggregated evaluation reveals hidden disparities.

items.stem: Which TWO are honest statements about bias mitigation? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Mitigations often trade some accuracy for improved fairness
options.rationale: Correct: trade-offs are common and should be stated.

options.text: A mitigation must be validated on held-out subgroups to confirm it helped
options.rationale: Correct: you must verify the fix, not assume it.

options.text: Mitigation permanently fixes bias with no monitoring needed
Removing the protected attribute always removes bias

items.stem: Why monitor for bias after deploying a mitigation?

options.text: Data and behaviour drift, so a fix can degrade over time
options.rationale: Correct: fairness is not static and must be watched.

options.text: Monitoring makes the model more accurate
options.rationale: Monitoring detects; it does not improve accuracy.
